newsitem.title: USA: Space shuttle countdown on track.
newsitem.headline: Space shuttle countdown on track.

text.p: NASA said on Tuesday there were no apparent obstacles to an on-time launch for the space shuttle Atlantis on a supply run to Russia's Mir space station.

"I'm happy to say everything is going smoothly so far," shuttle test director John Guidi told a news conference, adding that controllers had not detected any technical problems and the weather looked favourable for a blastoff before dawn on Thursday.
Forecasters gave the shuttle an 80 percent chance of fair weather for launch during a short seven-minute launch window that opens at 4:08 a.m. EDT (0808 GMT).
Atlantis was to dock with the orbiting Russian space station on Friday night to pick up U.S. astronaut Jerry Linenger and drop off his replacement, Mike Foale.
The shuttle will also deliver nearly 4,000 lbs (8,800 kg) of supplies and equipment to Mir, including a new oxygen generator to replace a failed device.
The space station has suffered a string of mechanical breakdowns since Linenger arrived in January. The worst incident was a fire in February that filled the complex with choking smoke.
NASA approved a four-month stay aboard Mir for Foale after repairs were made to the station's life support systems.
The British-born astrophysicist will be the fourth American citizen to live on Mir.
